extracted.intended_audience: federal, state, tribal, and local emergency responders who will serve as Public Information Officers on Type III All-Hazards Incident Management Teams (AHIMT)
extracted.subtask_description: A Type III All-Hazards Public Information Officer professional development course describing duties, information operations, media/community relations, safety, and transition/demobilization responsibilities for PIOs assigned to AHIMTs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course application and prerequisite documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must complete an AHIMT Course Application for this course and return it to TEMA.Training@tn.gov and attach all prerequisite documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach all prerequisite documentation to the AHIMT Course Application before submission; application is required for enrollment/verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course goal / target outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide federal, state, tribal, and local-level emergency responders with an overview of key duties and responsibilities of a Public Information Officer in a Type III All-Hazards Incident Management Team (AHIMT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the overall aim of the course and what learners should expect to gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum passing requirement for IACET CEU
rubrics_metrics.description: The learner must achieve a minimum passing score of 75% on final knowledge assessments or demonstrate mastery on performance assessments or research assignments to earn the IACET CEU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing may be demonstrated either via knowledge assessment (≥75%) or through demonstrated mastery on performance tasks or research assignments; meeting one of these is required to receive continuing education credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIMS ICS Position-Specific training / selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMS ICS Position Specific training shall be completed by personnel who will be required to gain a certificate of training and the credentials to function in an ICS Organization (e.g., IMT) as a member of the Command, General Staff or as a Unit Leader. This criteria will be verified on the student enrollment request by endorsement of the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) such as the State/Tribal Training Officer or the course manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrollment requires verification (endorsement) from the AHJ that the student is expected to function in the referenced ICS roles; intended to ensure only personnel who need the credential attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACE credit level and hours
rubrics_metrics.description: ACE: Level: Lower Division/Associate; ACE: Credit Hours: 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies academic credit equivalency awarded for completion of the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: TLETA POST approval
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates course meets Tennessee Law Enforcement Training Academy (TLETA) POST approval for the listed year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission area designation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified under the 'Respond' mission area of emergency management, informing scope and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required prerequisite courses
rubrics_metrics.description: The required prerequisites to this course are: IS-0100 An Introduction to the Incident Command System, ICS 100; IS-0200 Basic Incident Command System for Initial Response, ICS 200; E/L/G 0300 Intermediate Incident Command System for Expanding Incidents, ICS 300; E/L/G 0400 Advanced Incident Command System for Complex Incidents, ICS 400; IS-0700 An Introduction to the National Incident Management System; IS-0800 National Response Framework (NRF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students must have completed these specified FEMA/NIMS courses prior to enrollment; verification should be attached to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended training
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended: O-305, Type 3 AHIMT Training course (delivered by USFA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not mandatory but recommended background to augment course learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Describe PIO role and importance (initial operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the role and importance of the Public Information Officer position in incident operations, especially as it pertains to initial incident operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learner should be able to articulate PIO responsibilities and significance during the first stages of an incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Describe fundamentals of information operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the fundamentals of information operations during incident management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers core principles and processes of collecting, verifying, approving, and disseminating incident information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Develop a communications strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a communications strategy for disseminating incident information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learners are expected to produce or outline strategies for messaging, audiences, channels, timing, and coordination during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Explain media relations and social media role
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the importance of effective media relations, including social media, and the role of the Public Information Officer in developing and maintaining such relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes understanding best practices for interacting with traditional media and managing social media presence and messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Describe Assistant PIO roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the roles and responsibilities of Assistant Public Information Officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies delegation, support functions, and expected duties of assistant PIOs within an information unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Establish and leverage community relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the Public Information Officer may establish and leverage effective community relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers strategies for building trust, outreach, and engaging community stakeholders before, during, and after incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Handle special situations within incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the role of the Public Information Officer as it pertains to handling special situations within incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses atypical, sensitive, or complex communication scenarios (e.g., fatalities, criminal elements, cultural sensitivities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Safety for PIOs and escorts
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how Public Information Officers can keep themselves, and those they escort and work with, safe in the incident environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers situational awareness, protective measures, coordination with operations/safety officers, and limitations on access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: PIO roles during transition and demobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the Public Information Officer's roles and responsibilities during incident transition and demobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes messaging and activities related to handover, scaling down operations, and post-incident communications.
